unit.title: Preparing for the Oral History Interview

contentBlocks.text: You have questions and listening skills ready. Before capturing anyone's real ਯਾਦਾਂ (memories), one thing must come first: their genuine ਇਜਾਜ਼ਤ (permission).

Before recording any real interview, always ask clear ਇਜਾਜ਼ਤ first — explain what you're doing (a school project turning their story into a short documentary) and confirm they're comfortable being recorded, in plain, respectful language. This matters doubly with a ਬਜ਼ੁਰਗ (elder) sharing personal ਯਾਦਾਂ: their ਕਹਾਣੀ belongs to them, and treating it with genuine respect — including the right to skip a question or stop at any point — is part of doing this project honestly. Write, in Punjabi, a short, respectful sentence you could actually say to ask your elder's permission before starting.
You now have every piece needed to conduct your real interview respectfully and well. Tomorrow we'll review the whole process together with a mock interview.

objectives: Explain why asking genuine consent before recording matters, especially for personal memories
Write a real, respectful Punjabi sentence requesting permission to record
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's question list and listening skills.
2. Introduce the importance of genuine consent before recording, including the right to skip or stop.
3. Have the child write their own permission-request sentence in Punjabi.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review and mock interview.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a simple sentence template to adapt rather than requiring the child to construct one from scratch
Ready for more: ask them to also explain what they'd do if their elder wanted to skip a specific question — a genuine, respectful response to plan for in advance
Every Gurmukhi word used in this lesson was checked against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Genuine consent matters because the elder's story belongs to them, and recording without clear permission would be disrespectful. 2. A respectful permission request explains the project's purpose and confirms comfort with being recorded, including the right to skip or stop at any point.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'oral-history capstone' description, establishing the ethical foundation (genuine consent, respect for the elder's ownership of their story) a real documentary project requires.
